title: The Power of Habit
author: Charles Duhigg
blurb: Charles Duhigg, an investigative journalist, explains why habits form and how they can be changed. Drawing on neuroscience and real stories, he shows that much of what we do each day runs on automatic. Every habit follows a three-part loop: a cue, a routine, and a reward. A craving for the reward is what powers the loop. Duhigg argues that habits are hard to erase. Instead, we can keep the old cue and reward and swap in a new routine. Belief, often built inside a group, helps the change stick. He then moves from individuals to companies and communities. He shows how small keystone habits can trigger wide change, and how willpower itself can be trained into a habit. His message is hopeful. Once you understand how a habit works, you gain the power to reshape it.

lessons.b: Much of what we do each day is habit rather than conscious choice, as shown by a man with severe memory loss who still formed new routines without remembering them.

lessons.t: The Habit Loop: Cue, Routine, Reward
lessons.b: Every habit is a three-step loop in which a cue triggers a routine that delivers a reward, and the brain turns this loop into an automatic chunk to save effort.
Habits become powerful when we start to crave the reward in advance, which is how Febreze only took off once people anticipated a fresh-smelling finish to cleaning.
